answer: A reputation registry can require each agent to post a refundable stake before it can influence shared decisions. Its signal is earned through completed jobs: counterparties attest to delivery, and proven fraud triggers slashing of the stake and removal of accumulated reputation. An attacker can forge many identities, but cannot cheaply give each one credible history; funding and operating every stake ties up capital, while a detected lie risks losing it. Even an opal-bright new identity starts with no trusted record.
